(Canton, Ohio) | college = [[Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball|Bowling Green]] (1998–2002) | draft_year = 2002 | career_start = 2002 | career_end = 2014 | career_number = 4, 25, 20 | career_position = [[Point guard]] | years1 = 2002 | team1 = Saint Joseph Express | years2 = 2002–2003 | team2 = [[Basket Livorno|Mabo Prefabbricati Livorno]] | years3 = {{nbay|2003|full=y}} | team3 = [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] | years4 = 2004 | team4 = [[Yakima Sun Kings]] | years5 = 2004 | team5 = [[Pallacanestro Virtus Roma|Lottomatica Virtus Roma]] | years6 = {{nbay|2004|start}}–{{nbay|2005|end}} | team6 = [[Utah Jazz]] | years7 = {{nbay|2006|full=y}} | team7 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years8 = {{nbay|2006|end}} | team8 = [[Indiana Pacers]] | years9 = 2008 | team9 = [[Mens Sana Basket|Montepaschi Siena]] | years10 = 2008–2010 | team10 = [[Albuquerque Thunderbirds]] | years11 = 2010–2011 | team11 = [[Panionios B.C.|Panionios]] | years12 = 2011–2012 | team12 = [[Canton Charge]] | years13 = 2012 | team13 = [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] | years14 = 2012–2013 | team14 = [[BC Kalev/Cramo]] | years15 = 2013–2014 | team15 = [[LF Basket Norrbotten]] | highlights = * [[Mid-American Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|MAC Player of the Year]] (2002) * First-team All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] (2002) | bbr = mcleoke01 }} '''Keith McLeod''' (born November 5, 1979) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and current varsity boys basketball head coach at East Canton High School in Canton, Ohio. He is {{height|ft=6|in=2}} tall. He has also played in the [[NBA]] for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], [[Utah Jazz]], [[Golden State Warriors]] and [[Indiana Pacers]], in the [[Continental Basketball Association|CBA]] for the [[Yakima Sun Kings]], in the [[United States Basketball League|USBL]] for the [[Saint Joseph Express]], in the [[NBA D-League]] with the [[Albuquerque Thunderbirds]], [[Canton Charge]], and [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]], and in the [[Italy|Italian]] [[Serie A (basketball)|top league]] for [[Basket Livorno|Mabo Prefabbricati Livorno]], [[Pallacanestro Virtus Roma|Lottomatica Virtus Roma]] and [[Mens Sana Basket|Montepaschi Siena]]. ==College career== In 2001, he was named in the All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] second-team.{{cite web | url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/bgu/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/06mg.pdf | title=Falcon Scrapbook | publisher=CBs College Sports | access-date=May 13, 2015 | archive-date=May 18, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518092928/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/bgu/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/06mg.pdf | url-status=dead }} McLeod was the 2002 [[Mid-American Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|MAC men's basketball player of the year]], leading the [[Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball|Bowling Green]] to the [[Mid-American Conference men's basketball tournament|MAC championship game]] and a berth in the [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT]].{{cite web | url=http://www.toledoblade.com/Opinion/2005/02/10/McLeod-is-making-his-mark-with-Jazz.html | title=McLeod is making his mark with Jazz | publisher=toledoblade.com | date=February 10, 2005 | access-date=13 May 2015}} At the time of his graduation he was the school's second all-time leading scorer with 1,895 points. ==Professional career== He was not taken in the [[2002 NBA draft]], but was selected in the 2002 USBL Draft by the Saint Joseph Express, and in the 2002 CBA Draft by the Yakima Sun Kings. He was traded by the Jazz on July 13, 2006, to the [[Golden State Warriors]] - along with [[Devin Brown]] and [[Andre Owens]] - for [[Derek Fisher]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2517633 Jazz re-sign Harpring, complete trade for Fisher - NBA - ESPN] On January 17, 2007, McLeod was dealt to the [[Indiana Pacers]] along with teammates [[Mike Dunleavy Jr.]], [[Ike Diogu]] and [[Troy Murphy]] for [[Stephen Jackson]], [[Al Harrington]], [[Sarunas Jasikevicius]] and [[Josh Powell]].{{cite web |url=http://www.mopsquad.com/artman2/publish/Indiana_Pacers_72/Pacers_Warriors_announce_8-player_deal.htm |title=Pacers, Warriors announce 8-player deal |publisher=Associated Press |date=2007-01-17 |access-date = 2007-12-23}} On July 11, 2008, McLeod signed a one-year deal with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3483684 Acquired from the Nets in February, Wright re-signs with Mavs - NBA - ESPN] He was waived by the Mavericks on October 23, 2008 (before ever playing a game for them), and later played for the [[Albuquerque Thunderbirds]] of the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]]. McLeod never made his way back into the NBA and his final game was played on April 18, 2007, during his time with the Pacers. On that day, the Pacers lost to the [[Washington Wizards]] with McLeod recording 11 points, 4 rebounds, and 3 assists. On September 1, 2010, McLeod signed a 1-year deal with the Greek club [[Panionios B.C.]] McLeod signed with the [[Canton Charge]] of the [[NBA D-League]] in 2011.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/mcleod_peterson_111020.html NBA Development League: Canton Native Keith McLeod and Jamine Peterson Sign with Canton Charge] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150201082405/http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/mcleod_peterson_111020.html |date=2015-02-01 }} He was later traded to the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]]. In October 2012, McLeod joined [[BC Kalev/Cramo]] of Estonia[http://www.bckalev.ee/full_uudis.php?action=fullnews&showcomments=1&id=229 Homme saabub Tallinnasse BC Kalev/Cramo uus mängujuht!]{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} and poured in 25 points in his first game in the VTB League for the club, including a game winning basket at the buzzer. [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8m51ovP4rCs Keith McLeod's Game Winning Buzzerbeater ] On June 13, 2016, McLeod agreed to become an assistant to head coach Matt Hackenberg on the Canton Glenoak High School boys varsity basketball team. His primary focus will be on player development with the Golden Eagles. ==Education== McLeod attended [[Canton McKinley High School]] and graduated with a BS in Computer Science from Bowling Green State University. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== * {{Basketballstats |nba= 2693 |bbr= m/mcleoke01 }} {{Mid-American Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:McLeod, Keith}} [[Category:1979 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Albuquerque Thunderbirds players]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Estonia]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Greece]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Italy]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Sweden]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basket Livorno players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Canton, Ohio]] [[Category:BC Kalev/Cramo players]] [[Category:Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball players]] [[Category:Canton Charge players]] [[Category:Erie BayHawks (2008–2017) players]] [[Category:Golden State Warriors players]] [[Category:Indiana Pacers players]] [[Category:Korvpalli Meistriliiga players]] [[Category:Mens Sana Basket players]] [[Category:Minnesota Timberwolves players]] [[Category:Virtus Roma players]] [[Category:Panionios B.C. players]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Undrafted NBA players]] [[Category:Utah Jazz players]] [[Category:Yakima Sun Kings players]] [[Category:McKinley High School (Canton, Ohio) alumni]]
